terms.definition: a system that perceives the state of its environment and produces an action to take in it, in a loop
what the agent does (an action) and what the environment returns afterward (an observation), which becomes part of the next state
running agent-issued code and commands inside an isolated container rather than on the host machine, so a mistake cannot damage the user's own system
OpenHands' chronological record of every past action and observation, which forms the agent's working state
the specific set of tools/commands exposed to an agent for acting on its environment; a better-designed ACI can change performance independently of the underlying LLM
OpenHands' library of Python-function tools that are auto-imported into the agent's code-execution environment
OpenHands' collection of implemented, ready-to-use agents (CodeActAgent, Browsing Agent, GPTSwarm agent, micro agents, etc.)
OpenHands' default generalist agent, which acts by executing code (bash, Python, or a browser DSL) rather than by issuing fixed, pre-defined tool calls
one agent handing off a subtask to a second, more specialized agent
the percentage of SWE-Bench task instances for which the agent's patch makes the issue's hidden test suite pass
the percentage of task instances an agent solves within a single attempt
whether the agent is given zero or one full worked example (a demonstration trajectory) before attempting the task
a benchmark of real GitHub issues an agent must resolve by editing a repository so a hidden test suite passes; Lite is a 300-instance subset
a benchmark of 164 Python functions with an inserted bug that the agent must fix using the provided test cases
a self-hostable benchmark of 812 realistic web tasks (shopping, forums, developer platforms, content management)
a suite of 125 small, synthetic web-interface tasks with shorter horizons than WebArena
a benchmark of 466 real-world assistant tasks requiring reasoning, web browsing, and sometimes multi-modal understanding
a graduate-level, 'Google-proof' multiple-choice science question benchmark
a multi-turn benchmark whose OS subset requires an agent to complete tasks by interacting directly with an operating system via bash
a multi-turn benchmark that gives an agent up to five rounds of tool use with GPT-4-simulated natural-language feedback, on math and code subsets
a synthetic deductive-reasoning benchmark; the hardest subset used here requires 5-hop reasoning chains
a 20-Questions-style benchmark where an agent deduces a hidden entity through strategic yes/no questioning
